result.title: Why Linear Models Can Still Work in a Complex and Changing World
result.summary: Linear models can predict well in complex domains even when underlying mechanisms are nonlinear. We argue that this can occur because the complexity of the world exceeds the complexity that can be learned reliably from finite, partially observed data. Flexible models can exploit curvature, thresholds, and interactions that fit one hospital, period, population, policy setting, or measurement process but fail elsewhere. When this instability lies mainly in the nonlinear component, omitting it can give linear models lower prediction error in a new environment. We connect this claim to work on simple linear rules, bias and variance, regularization, best linear prediction, measurement error, distribution shift, invariance, Rashomon sets, and underspecification. Proposition 1 gives a simple squared-error case in which a nonlinear rule learned in the training environment raises target error because it transfers too weakly; finite-sample estimation error can strengthen this result. Partial observation alone is not enough: the link between observed variables and unobserved factors must vary across environments. Stable nonlinear structure favors flexible models, and linear models remain vulnerable to linear spurious relationships. Model complexity should therefore be chosen by cross-environment stability as well as training-data accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 论文论证在复杂且不断变化的世界里，由于数据有限且只被部分观测，灵活模型学到的非线性成分往往难以跨环境迁移，省略它反而能让线性模型在新环境中获得更低的预测误差，并提出应以跨环境稳定性而非仅训练精度来选择模型复杂度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于不变性、欠定性、Rashomon 集与跨环境稳定性的论证，可能为判断 VLM 内部 latent 推理状态是学到了可迁移结构还是环境特异的虚假关联提供分析视角，可供核查。
